sentences.text: These appeals arise out of an accident on 17.06.2016 which is not in dispute.
2. The liability of insurer to pay the compensation is also not in dispute.

3. The appellant in M.F.A. No.3473/2018 is dissatisfied with a compensation of Rs.1,57,090/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
4. The Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 14% which, in my view, is just and proper.

However, the Tribunal has adopted the notional income of claimant at Rs.8,000/- which would have to be disturbed and the notional income of NC: 2024:KHC:51016 Rs.9,500/- will have to be applied in light of the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
5. Furthermore, the Tribunal has committed an error in adopting the multiplier of '5' when it ought to have adopted the multiplier of '7', as the claimant was 65 years old.

In light of above, the claimant is entitled to Rs.1,11,720/- (9,500/- x 12 x '7' x 14%) towards 'loss of future income'.
6.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings', in my view, this would have to be enhanced to Rs.60,000/-.
7. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'loss of amenities'.
Having regard to the fact that the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 14%, it would be appropriate to award Rs.60,000/- under the said head.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.23,989/- towards 'medical expenses' and the same is just and proper and is accordingly affirmed.
9. The claimant was hospitalized for four days and consequently, the sum of Rs.7,000/- awarded towards 'conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges' would have to be enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.

Hence, the claimant is entitled to Rs.38,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 4 months) under the said head.
